body.text: On November 4, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev awarded Rustam Emomali the Order for Selfless Service (Fidokorona Xizmatlari Uchun) “for his significant contributions to strengthening the strategic partnership and alliance between the two countries, as well as his fruitful work in expanding interparliamentary dialogue.”

Emomali was on an official visit to Tashkent and also stopped off in Bukhara. He’s chair of Tajikistan’s National Assembly, the appointed mayor of Dushanbe, and, oh yes, son of President Emomali Rahmon – a detail Uzbek and Tajik press coverage of the visit failed to mention.

Of course, everyone knows whose son Emomali is, no need to remark on it. Except there is. Emomali is the most likely next president of Tajikistan. The country is due for an election by October 2027 and has been cleared of all serious political opposition. Rahmon, 74, has been president of Tajikistan since 1994 – 32 years.

For the last decade speculation has run rampant that Rahmon would, at a time of his choosing, step down and cede the presidency to his son. That speculation took on a serious tone in 2016, when Tajikistan held a referendum on amendments to the constitution, one of which served to lower the age requirement for the presidency from 35 to 30. At the time, the next presidential election was set for 2020, when Emomali would be 32. Convenient.
In 2017, Emomali was appointed mayor of Dushanbe by his father, a clear elevation of the son into the political spotlight.

As it turned out, 2020 was hardly a good time for even a carefully managed political transition, given the COVID-19 pandemic. Nevertheless, in April 2020, Emomali was named chair of Tajikistan’s National Assembly, the Majlisi Milli. That positioned him, constitutionally, as second-in-line to the presidency. When the presidential election came and went in October of that year, Rahmon remained at the top.

Last year, speculation bubbled up again as Dushanbe dispatched Emomali to Moscow, for his first official one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. At the time, journalist Bruce Pannier said in an interview with RFE/RL’s Tajik Service, Radio Ozodi, that the visit itself held significance.

“In the case of Tajikistan, Moscow’s support is crucial even before a transfer of power can take place,” he said, noting that Russia maintains a military base in Tajikistan and is one of the country’s largest trading partners. “If Moscow doesn’t approve the process, it could seriously complicate the situation for both Emomali Rahmon and any other contender for power. That’s why the Kremlin’s support is critical — both for the transfer of power itself and for its future sustainability.”

After Russia, one of Tajikistan’s most important relationships in the region is with Uzbekistan. What once was a relationship marred by tension has evolved significantly since the 2016 death of Islam Karimov, who famously (or infamously) didn’t get along with most of his neighbors and certainly not Tajikistan. But in 2018, 17 years after his last official visit, Rahmon visited Tashkent and Samarkand and the relationship entered a new, positive era.

According to the younger Emomali’s press statements, his meeting with Mirziyoyev focused on the “the current state and prospects for the development of friendly relations and strategic partnership” between Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.”

The Uzbek presidential press service characterized the meeting as addressing “key issues concerning the further deepening of Uzbek-Tajik relations of friendship, good-neighborliness, strategic partnership, and alliance, including through interparliamentary cooperation.”
Emomali also met with Tanzila Narbayeva, the chairwoman of Uzbekistan’s Senate, and the two signed a road map for interparliamentary cooperation for 2027-2028.

As Tajikistan once again moves toward presidential elections, Central Asia watchers the world over will be discussing whether 2027 is finally the year Tajikistan follows its neighbors into a managed political transition. It’ll be important to keep tabs on Emomali as the election approaches.

There is one more critical relationship for Tajikistan: China. In 2023, Emomali made an official visit to Beijing – though he did not meet personally with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. In 2024, Xi traveled to Dushanbe for a state visit. Although Emomali did not meet personally with Xi then either, he was shown prominently in media coverage standing beside his father in bidding Xi farewell at the airport.
